title: I don't need an AI agent to be an executive assistant. I need it to be a wife.
key_facts: A Business Insider writer argues she wants an AI agent that acts like 'a wife', anticipating needs, rather than a task-doer.
She is answering a post that went viral earlier this week by marketing entrepreneur and podcaster Sonia Baschez, who said Silicon Valley keeps building 'a husband' when she wants 'a wife'.
Baschez wants an agent that anticipates her needs rather than doing one-off tasks like booking flights.
The writer says she mostly uses agents (she has tested Muse most) for family paperwork and scheduling, but still has to give step-by-step instructions.
She admits the metaphor plays on gendered stereotypes; Baschez says the same.
She is now testing Muse, Instinct and Dot and jokes she has too many 'wives' nagging her.
quote_evidence: Sonia Baschez, a marketing entrepreneur and podcaster, went viral earlier this week for saying what she wanted from AI agents is "a wife," not "a husband."
why_it_matters_hint: Describes what ordinary users want from AI agents: anticipation, not just instruction-following.
event_date: Baschez post earlier in the week of 5 Oct 2026; essay 9 Oct 2026
notes: Opinion essay by an unnamed writer; the Baschez post itself was not read.
